chunks: Through this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Munqari, from Asad ibn Abi Al'a, from Hisham ibn Ahmar, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I wanted to ask him about al-Mufaddal ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. He was in his estate on a day of intense heat, and sweat was flowing down his chest. He initiated the conversation and said: Yes, by the God, except whom there is no god, the man is al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ja'fi. Yes, by the God, except whom there is no god, the man (he is) al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ja'fi. Until I counted thirty-seven times he repeated it, and he said: Indeed, he is father after father.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُفَضَّلُ بْنُ عُمَرَ الْجَعْفِيُّ: Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ja'fi, a prominent companion of the Imams
key_terms.وَالِدٌ بَعْدَ وَالِدٍ: Father after father, indicating a man of outstanding virtue or a lineage of excellence

ai.seo_question: Who is al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ja'fi and what did Imam al-Sadiq say about him?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) spontaneously confirms the identity of al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ja'fi as a trusted emissary, repeating his affirmation over thirty times to emphasize his reliability and high status. The phrase 'father after father' (walad ba'da walad) highlights a lineage of virtue or exceptional character, underscoring the Imam's deep trust in him during the Minor Ghayba. This incident serves as a key proof for the authenticity of the emissaries (al-Nuwwab al-Arba'a) who conveyed the Imam's decrees to the Shia community.
